chose: The endings that close a sentence (-아요/어요, -아/어, -지요, -지, -네요, -네, -(으)ㄹ까요?, -(으)ㄹ까?, -(으)세요) join the construction catalogue as a second kind of entry, `closing`, beside the twenty `joining` ones, with stable ids under `close.`. Each names its register (해요 or 반말) and the sentence moods it can end, so a phrase that joins two clauses can be checked end to end: a joining ending's refused moods against the closing ending's. Conjugation's ad-hoc "polite" ending is retired into `close.ayo.plain`, and the catalogue is now the only list of endings. The phrase shelf (KP3, #2852) needs these to rebuild a whole expression; the grades stay "unchecked" as C1085 has them.
options: closing endings as a second kind in the one construction catalogue, typed by `kind` (taken)
a separate list of sentence endings beside the catalogue
keep conjugation's single "polite" ending and add more such special cases
